What a lie. Dungeons and Dragons is increasing in popularity because it's being marketed well and the commitment aspect is lower. Pick up and play groups like Adventure's League and 1 shots are the driving force in bringing more players into the game.

The face to face interaction was always there, but 4th ed was and is a miniatures game more than any other edition. AD&D (80s dnd) and 3rd edition (90s dnd) both had heavy roll playing focuses, but 3rd edition slipped into a power-gaming trap (like JRPGs) at higher levels. The simple fact is 5th edition and AD&D are incredibly similar, but 5th edition is a little simpler. So what changed? An idea that you can take 1 character to multiple tables. Now people don't need to schedule around 5 people's lives to crawl through a dungeon. They can just show up on Xday and sit down at a table and play with whoever shows up. The DM reads a 20 page story and walks the players through one 2 to 4 hour session. It's not a 12 hour all day event every Saturday.

Community, big bang theory and Stranger Things have put D&D into the public mind. High production live streamed or vloged D&D campaigns (e.g. Acquisition's Incorporated, Critical Role) have shown how dynamic and fun it can be for a group of friends. And in truth the community just has a larger willingness to communicate with new people. D&D isn't a dirty secret now, it's something people talk about.

The women also were always there. I've played with about 40% women players my entire life. I've had some games with all guys, mainly in middle and high school. But women still wanted to play even in high school.
